title: Goals: amount, date and monthly step
blurb: Meena wants a used laptop for her course. Turn the wish into a goal and work out how many months it takes.
t1.title: A wish becomes a goal
t1.hook: Meena wants a used laptop that costs {target}. She says, 'I will save for it someday.' Her teacher asks: how much, by when, and how much each month?
t1.define: A **goal** is a wish with three parts: an amount, a date and a **monthly step**. Without them it is only a wish.
t1.analogy: A goal is like a ladder. The amount is the top. The monthly step is each rung. Count the rungs and you know the date.
q1.prompt: Which one is a real goal?
q1.hint: Look for an amount, a date and a monthly step.
q1.explain: A goal names the amount, the date and the monthly step. The others are wishes.
q1.opt.a: I want to save more money
q1.fb.a: That is a wish. It has no amount, no date and no monthly step, so you cannot tell if you are on track.
q1.opt.b: I will have {target} by next March, saving {monthly} a month
q1.opt.c: I hope to buy a laptop someday
q2.prompt: Meena wants the {target} laptop in {wishMonths} months. How much must she set aside each month? Type a number.
q2.hint: Divide the amount by the number of months.
q2.explain: {target} divided by {wishMonths} months is {monthlyNeeded} a month.
t2.title: How many months?
t2.formula: Months to reach a goal = goal amount ÷ monthly step, rounded up to a whole month.
t2.steps.3: Divide, then round up to the next whole month
t2.note: Round up. If the answer is ten and a half, you are still short after ten months, so you need one more.
q3.prompt: Meena can put aside {monthly} a month. How many months to reach {target}? Type a number.
q4.prompt: Another month she can only manage {partial}. How many whole months now? Round up.
q4.explain: {target} divided by {partial} leaves a part month, and rounding up gives {months2} months.
t3.title: Lab: what a bigger step does
t3.explore: Open the lab. Change the monthly step and watch the months to goal change.
q5.prompt: In the lab, set the monthly step to {fast}. How many months to reach {target}? Type a number.
q5.hint: Read the Months to goal box.
q6.prompt: What happens to the months if Meena doubles her monthly step?
q6.hint: Try {monthly} and then double it in the lab.
q6.explain: Doubling the step roughly halves the months.
t4.title: When it is too slow
t4.define: If the plan is too slow, you have three levers. Save more each month, wait longer, or pick a cheaper goal.
t4.note: Meena needs the laptop in {deadline} months. At {monthly} a month, that is too soon. She must pull one of the three levers.
q7.prompt: With {monthly} a month for {deadline} months, how much can Meena reach? That is the price of a cheaper laptop she can afford. Type a number.
q7.hint: Multiply the monthly step by the months.
q8.prompt: Her plan takes more months than she has. Which change can close the gap?
q8.hint: Look back at the three levers.
q8.explain: Saving more, waiting longer or choosing a cheaper laptop each change the sum.
q8.fb.a: Saving more is one lever, not the only one. A later date or a cheaper goal also close the gap.
q8.opt.b: Any of the three: save more, wait longer, or pick a cheaper laptop
q8.opt.c: Nothing, she must drop the goal
q8.opt.d: Hope the price falls by itself
t5.title: Challenge
t5.note: Say Meena already has {head} saved from tutoring. That is a head start. Only the rest needs a monthly step.
q9.prompt: She has {head} saved and puts aside {monthly} a month. How many months to reach {target}? Type a number.
q9.hint: Take the head start off the price first, then divide.
q9.explain: {target} minus {head} is {remaining}. Divided by {monthly}, that is {months4} months.
glossary.plan_goal.def: A wish with an amount, a date and a monthly step.
glossary.plan_monthly_step.def: The amount you put aside each month towards a goal.
